B01.statement: At the start of Buffer.Read, lastRead is assigned opInvalid.
B01.reason: The assignment at the start of Buffer.Read sets lastRead to opInvalid.

B02.statement: At the start of Buffer.Read, lastRead is assigned opRead.
B02.reason: The assignment at the start of Buffer.Read sets lastRead to opInvalid, a different value from opRead.

B03.statement: The cited assignment guarantees that the buffer can never contain unread bytes.
B03.reason: The assignment sets lastRead and gives no information about whether the buffer contains unread bytes.

B04.statement: After a ReadByte succeeds, Read(nil) occurs and then UnreadByte succeeds.
B04.reason: The assignment establishes neither the sequence of calls nor whether UnreadByte succeeds.

B05.statement: Buffer.ReadByte returns io.EOF when no byte is available.
B05.fragment: If no byte is available, it returns error [io.EOF].
B05.reason: The comment documents io.EOF for this condition. The quoted fragment contains no executable return.
